prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universally “best” interior painting company in St. Louis — the right contractor depends on your needs (residential vs. commercial), budget, schedule, surfaces/repairs needed, and the level of finish you want. I can help you find the best fit. Here’s how to pick one and what to expect.

How to find the best company for your job
- Define your priorities: price, speed, premium materials/finish, eco‑friendly paints, or extensive surface repair.
- Sources to find candidates: Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, Houzz, Nextdoor, and the Better Business Bureau.
- Get at least 3 written estimates with the same scope of work so you can compare apples to apples.

What to check for each company
- Insurance: and ask for proof of general liability and workers’ compensation.
- References: recent local projects and photos; follow up with references.
- Portfolio: photos of finished interiors similar to your job.
- Written estimate details: prep work, primer, number of coats, paint brand & sheen, protection of floors/furniture, caulking/patching, cleanup, timeline, and payment schedule.
- Warranty: workmanship warranty length and what it covers.
- Permits/registration: check local city requirements (some municipalities require contractor registration).

Typical price guidance (ballpark)
- Per room: often $300–$1,000+ depending on size and prep.
- Per square foot: roughly $1.50–$4.00 per sq. ft. for walls (wide range based on prep, ceilings, trim, and paint quality).
(Exact costs vary — get written estimates.)

Red flags
- Only takes cash or demands large upfront nonrefundable payment.
- No written contract or vague scope.
- Very low bid relative to others without explanation.
- No proof of insurance or unwillingness to provide references.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list of highly rated St. Louis interior painters (I can look up current reviews if you want me to search).
- Draft an interview/checklist or a template RFP to send to painters.
- Review estimates you receive and compare them.

Tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood, whether it’s a home or business, and any special needs (high ceilings, lots of trim, lead paint concerns, timeline, budget) and I’ll narrow down good local options.
